mechanism: IP3R-dependent ER Ca2+ depletion / cytosolic Ca2+ overload (SH-SY5Y, Abeta42)
sentence: These findings suggest that ADRA1 drives STING activation via IP3R-mediated ER Ca2+ depletion and subsequent cytoplasmic Ca2+ dyshomeostasis.
justification: Non-canonical, cGAS-independent STING activation in neurons driven by IP3R-mediated ER Ca2+ release: calcium acts upstream of STING.

mechanism: FRET in BEAS-2B cells
sentence: The data confirmed that STIM1 and STING interacted in uninfected cells (Fig.
justification: Independent confirmation (FRET, human bronchial cells) of the STIM1–STING ER-retention complex.

mechanism: ER Ca2+ lowering by HRV 2B frees STING from STIM1
sentence: This data suggests that upon HRV infection, STING is released from STIM1 due to alterations in calcium homeostasis, which drives the binding of STING to PI4KIIIbeta and PI4P and recruitment to the RO.
justification: ER Ca2+ depletion (HRV 2B viroporin) releases STING from STIM1: store Ca2+ gates STING trafficking.

sentence: We further find that TMEM110 expression is restrained by the nucleic acid sensor STING under basal conditions, and that a naturally occurring interface mutation between TMEM110 and STING causes defective lysosomal DNA disposal and aberrant type I interferon activity.
justification: STING restrains expression of the SOCE regulator TMEM110/STIMATE, a feedback from DNA sensing onto a calcium-handling ER protein.

mechanism: interface mutation
sentence: We further find that TMEM110 expression is restrained by the nucleic acid sensor STING under basal conditions, and that a naturally occurring interface mutation between TMEM110 and STING causes defective lysosomal DNA disposal and aberrant type I interferon activity.
justification: A TMEM110(STIMATE)–STING interface exists and its mutation deregulates type I IFN: direct contact between a SOCE regulator and STING.

sentence: Mechanistically, SELENOK interacts with STING in the ER and promotes STING oligomerization, which in turn promotes its translocation from the ER to the Golgi.
justification: ER selenoprotein K (a regulator of Ca2+ flux) binds STING in the ER and licenses its oligomerization.

mechanism: promotes oligomerization and ER exit
sentence: SELENOK interacts with STING in the ER and promotes its oligomerization, thereby licensing STING trafficking to the Golgi complex.
justification: SELENOK is required for STING oligomerization and ER-to-Golgi trafficking, i.e. STING activation.

mechanism: mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake at MERCs
sentence: Inhibition of mitochondrial calcium uptake due to STING deficiency mitigates the aggregation of N-GSDMD and Drp1 on the mitochondrial membrane.
justification: STING controls ER–mitochondria (MERC) Ca2+ transfer, linking STING to mitochondrial calcium and pyroptosis.

sentence: We show that TMEM203 interacts, functionally cooperates, and comigrates with STING following cell stimulation, which in turn leads to the activation of the kinase TBK1, and the IRF3 transcription factor.
justification: TMEM203, an IP3R-interacting regulator of ER Ca2+, binds STING and drives its signalling.

mechanism: promotes STING translocation to endo-lysosomes
sentence: Here, we demonstrate that TMEM203, a protein that was recently shown to be endosomal and interacts with the pleiotropic inositol phosphate signaling pathway protein IP3R, is associated with SLE disease activity, forms a functional and ligand-dependent complex with STING, and promotes its translocation to endo-lysosomes.
justification: TMEM203 promotes STING translocation to endo-lysosomes and TBK1/IRF3 activation; relevant to SLE.

sentence: TMEM203 interacts with STING and STIM1.
justification: STIM1 binds TMEM203 as well as STING: a three-way competition at the ER.

mechanism: competition for STING binding (luciferase complementation)
sentence: 2I) and that STIM1 was able to disrupt the TMEM203/STING complex in a dose-dependent manner (Fig.
justification: STIM1 and TMEM203 compete for STING binding; STIM1 disrupts the activating TMEM203–STING complex.

mechanism: STING N154S in Jurkat T cells; UPR motif
sentence: Together, our data uncover a critical IFN-independent function of STING that regulates calcium homeostasis, ER stress, and T cell survival.
justification: SAVI gain-of-function STING disrupts T-cell Ca2+ homeostasis independently of IFN, a direct STING-to-calcium link.

mechanism: STIM1 aa1-249 retains STING in the ER
sentence: To corroborate with the N154S/RRDD finding, we ectopically expressed STIM1 (aa1-249) in Jurkat N154S cells to block STING trafficking, and we found that it also significantly reduced ER stress and cell death (Fig.
justification: The STIM1 N-terminal fragment blocks STING trafficking and rescues ER stress / T-cell death caused by a SAVI STING mutant.

mechanism: keeps STIM1 dimeric, primes translocation to cortical ER (HEK-293T)
sentence: We therefore propose that UNC93B1 is a chaperone that facilitates STIM1 early activation steps associated with ER Ca2+ depletion to enable the switch into an extended conformation required for the efficient trapping of Orai1 channels.
justification: UNC93B1, the TLR trafficking chaperone, keeps STIM1 primed for SOCE: an innate-immunity protein tuning the STIM1 Ca2+ sensor.

mechanism: ER Ca2+ release in liver macrophages after hypoxia/reoxygenation
sentence: We demonstrated that STING increases intracellular calcium in liver macrophages to promote pyroptosis, which leads to an increase in liver inflammation and tissue injury in liver IRI, and calcium promoted by STING in this process may be mainly released from the ER.
justification: STING raises cytosolic Ca2+ in Kupffer cells, mostly by ER release, driving caspase-1/GSDMD pyroptosis: a STING-to-calcium effector arm.

mechanism: co-precipitation in THP1 macrophages
sentence: Moreover, we observed that the stimulation-induced dissociation of STING from STIM1, reported to enable STING activation, was inhibited by ISD017 (Fig.
justification: The STIM1-STING complex in human THP1 macrophages is pharmacologically targetable: the ISD017 peptide locks STING onto STIM1.

mechanism: ER retention, ER-to-Golgi trafficking blocked
sentence: Collectively, ISD017 blocks STING at the ER level through a mechanism dependent on STIM1.
justification: STIM1 is the ER retention factor through which an antagonist blocks STING ER-to-Golgi exit; therapeutic angle for lupus.

mechanism: thapsigargin / ionomycin boost cGAMP-induced STING and IRF3 phosphorylation in primary human T cells
sentence: To this end, either Ionomycin, which acts as a Ca2+ ionophore at the plasma and ER membranes, or Thapsigargin, which depletes ER Ca2+ levels by inhibiting the ER Ca2+-ATPase, were able to potently boost STING and IRF3 phosphorylation together with cGAMP.
justification: In human primary T cells, ER Ca2+ store depletion potentiates STING and IRF3 phosphorylation, placing store Ca2+ upstream of STING activation in the adaptive compartment.

mechanism: ORAI1/STIM1 knockout HEK293-ACE2 cells; resting cytoplasmic Ca2+
sentence: Collectively, by stable expression of ACE2 and deletion of ORAI1/STIM1, we developed a system to examine the role of ORAI1/STIM1 in the host response to SARS-CoV-2 infection and identified the role of ORAI1 in Ca2+ homeostasis in these cells.
justification: ORAI1 sets resting cytosolic Ca2+ and, through it, tonic type I IFN signalling and antiviral resistance: the SOCE pore feeding back on innate immunity.

mechanism: FRET in BEAS-2B cells; GSK'783 restores the STIM1-bound state
sentence: The pharmacological inhibition of STING during EV-D68 infection, using STING antagonist GSK'783, demonstrated that STING did not associate with PI4P but instead remained in the ER and associated with STIM1 (Figure 4B), confirming that EV-D68 interferes with STING canonical trafficking upon infection.
justification: FRET evidence that STING sits on STIM1 at rest and is pulled off it by EV-D68; a STING antagonist restores the STIM1-bound ER state.

mechanism: co-immunoprecipitation; STING(FTWAAS) is TRPV2-interaction deficient
sentence: While cGAS and its enzymatic product cGAMP are required for [Ca2+]i elevation after replication stress, STING normally associates with and represses TRPV2 to prevent unscheduled Ca2+ release in the absence of replication stress (Figures 4 and 5).
justification: STING directly binds the ER Ca2+ channel TRPV2: a second STING-calcium channel complex alongside STIM1, acting on the release side.

mechanism: STING depletion alone elevates [Ca2+]i
sentence: While cGAS mediates cytosDNA sensing and cGAMP production to promote TRPV2-mediated Ca2+ release from the ER after replication stress, STING normally represses TRPV2 activity to prevent unscheduled activation of the pathway in the absence of replication stress.
justification: Resting STING clamps TRPV2 shut, so STING loss raises cytosolic Ca2+: STING is a brake on ER Ca2+ release, mirroring STIM1 being a brake on STING.

mechanism: cGAMP binding dissociates the STING-TRPV2 complex
sentence: The subsequent binding of cGAMP to STING causes its dissociation from TRPV2, leading to TRPV2 derepression and Ca2+ release from the ER, which in turn activates the downstream signaling cascade to prevent fork degradation.
justification: cGAMP binding is the switch that releases TRPV2 from STING, converting DNA sensing into an ER Ca2+ release signal.

mechanism: ER Ca2+ release after hydroxyurea-induced replication stress
sentence: Together, these results strongly suggest that following cGAS activation, the binding of cGAMP to STING causes TRPV2 derepression and Ca2+ release to preserve chromosome stability after replication stress.
justification: TRPV2 is the channel that carries the STING-gated ER Ca2+ release, feeding CaMKK2/AMPK and replication-fork protection.

mechanism: PRRSV Nsp2 deubiquitinates and stabilizes STIM1, retaining STING at the ER (swine)
sentence: Mechanistically, PRRSV Nsp2 retains STING at the ER by increasing the level of Ca2+ sensor stromal interaction molecule 1 (STIM1) protein.
justification: An RNA virus exploits the STIM1 brake on STING: its protease stabilizes STIM1 to keep STING in the ER and blunt type I IFN, and STIM1 loss restricts the virus.

mechanism: STIM1 knockdown in HEL cells reduces STING exocytosis after HSV-1 infection
sentence: STING exocytosis was observed after infecting the parental cells, but reduced STING exocytosis was observed after infecting STIM1 KD derivatives (Fig.
justification: Beyond retaining STING in the ER, STIM1 is required for STING exocytosis during HSV-1 infection: a positive trafficking role that conflicts with the pure-brake model.

mechanism: thapsigargin-loaded nanozyme microneedles; ER Ca2+ depletion relieves STIM1 retention
sentence: HU inhibits DNA replication and repair, promoting cytosolic double-stranded DNA accumulation and activation of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway, while TG induces endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ depletion to relieve stromal interaction molecule 1 (STIM1)-mediated inhibition of STING trafficking, thereby amplifying type I interferon signaling.
justification: The STIM1 brake on STING is exploited therapeutically: depleting ER Ca2+ with thapsigargin releases STING trafficking and amplifies tumour type I IFN in vivo.

mechanism: co-immunoprecipitation in myeloid cells
sentence: Mechanistically, TMEM173 binding to ITPR1 controls calcium release from the endoplasmic reticulum in macrophages and monocytes.
justification: STING binds the IP3 receptor ITPR1 directly: a second STING-calcium channel complex, on the ER release side, driving coagulation in sepsis.

mechanism: ER Ca2+ release via ITPR1, independent of type I IFN
sentence: Mechanistically, TMEM173 binding to ITPR1 controls calcium release from the endoplasmic reticulum in macrophages and monocytes.
justification: Through ITPR1, STING controls ER Ca2+ release in myeloid cells, and this IFN-independent arm drives lethal coagulation.

mechanism: ITPR3 at MAMs; mitochondrial Ca2+ influx
sentence: Heavy MF up-regulated Piezo1 in PDLCs, reducing mitochondrial Ca2+ influx by inhibiting ITPR3 expression in mitochondria-associated membranes.
justification: ITPR3 at mitochondria-associated membranes sets mitochondrial Ca2+ influx, the upstream step of a calcium-to-STING arm.

mechanism: indirect: mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake -> mtDNA release into cytosol -> cGAS-STING
sentence: Decreased mitochondrial calcium uptake led to reduced cytoplasmic release of mitochondrial DNA and inhibited the activation of the cGAS-STING signaling cascade, subsequently inhibiting monocyte-to-osteoclast differentiation.
justification: Mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake gates cGAS-STING activation by controlling mtDNA release: an indirect calcium-to-STING route distinct from the STIM1 brake.

mechanism: direct interaction; modulates STING polymerization and trafficking
sentence: Here, we first report that ATP2A2 directly interacts with STING1, regulating STING1-mediated innate immune response by modulating its polymerization and trafficking, thereby inhibiting DNA virus infection.
justification: SERCA2/ATP2A2, the ER calcium pump, binds STING directly: a third calcium-machinery protein in physical contact with STING, after STIM1 and ITPR1.

mechanism: modulates polymerization and trafficking; required for SEC62-dependent reticulophagy
sentence: Here, we first report that ATP2A2 directly interacts with STING1, regulating STING1-mediated innate immune response by modulating its polymerization and trafficking, thereby inhibiting DNA virus infection.
justification: ATP2A2 governs STING polymerization and trafficking, placing the ER Ca2+ pump itself on the STING activation route.

mechanism: indirect: ER Ca2+ release and blocked efflux -> Ca2+ overload -> mtDNA release -> cGAS-STING (CT26 cells)
sentence: HAP promoted the release of intracellular Ca2+ stores in cancer cells, and curcumin inhibited Ca2+ efflux, resulting in intracellular Ca2+ overload and the release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA).
justification: Second, independent support for the indirect calcium-to-STING route: cytosolic Ca2+ overload damages mitochondria, releasing mtDNA that activates cGAS-STING in tumour cells.

mechanism: STING-independent; Ca2+-dependent ubiquitin recognition by TBC1D9 (HeLa, GAS infection)
sentence: We show that cytosolic Ca2+ signaling is required for TBK1 activation during xenophagy and mitophagy and this process is regulated by Ca2+-binding TBC1D9, highlighting TBC/RabGAP-mediated regulation of TBK1 activation in selective autophagy.
justification: Cytosolic Ca2+ activates TBK1 directly, through the Ca2+-binding protein TBC1D9 and independently of STING: a calcium entry point into innate immune signalling that bypasses the STIM1-STING brake.

mechanism: STING knockdown in obese rat atria; ER-to-mitochondria Ca2+ transfer
sentence: Interestingly, although STING activation is generally considered a downstream event of mitochondrial calcium overload and injury, our results show that knocking down STING can alleviate obesity-induced mitochondrial calcium overload and mitigate mitochondrial damage.
justification: STING is upstream of mitochondrial Ca2+ overload, not only downstream of it: knocking STING down relieves the overload, closing a feed-forward loop between calcium and DNA sensing.

mechanism: STIM1 D84G knock-in mice; constitutive SOCE in skeletal muscle
sentence: These data suggest that D84G STIM1 can spontaneously activate Orai1 channels in the T-tubular membrane.
justification: Direct functional evidence that STIM1 gates ORAI1, here constitutively: a gain-of-function STIM1 opens ORAI1 without store depletion, anchoring the canonical SOCE edge in primary tissue.

mechanism: indirect: ERO1A-driven ER-to-mitochondria Ca2+ shuttling at MAMs -> mtDNA release -> cGAS-STING
sentence: Blocking the Ero1alpha/MAMs/mtCa2+ axis suppresses mtDNA release and downregulates the cGAS-STING-NFkappaB signaling cascade, thus promoting M2 polarization and neural repair.
justification: Third independent support for the indirect route: blocking ER-to-mitochondria Ca2+ shuttling cuts mtDNA release and shuts down cGAS-STING, here switching macrophage phenotype after spinal cord injury.

mechanism: high-fat diet; MERC dysregulation and impaired Ca2+ homeostasis in mouse adipocytes
sentence: In summary, our study found that high-fat diet leads to structural and functional dysregulation of MERC in mouse adipocytes, resulting in ER stress and impaired calcium homeostasis, which induces interferon (IFN) responses centered on STING, as well as triggers insulin resistance.
justification: Fourth context for calcium feeding STING: in adipocytes, disrupted ER-mitochondria contacts and calcium homeostasis drive a STING-centred interferon response and insulin resistance.

mechanism: proteomics then co-IP in A498 and RCC10 renal carcinoma cells
sentence: Overall, these data suggest that the mitochondrial outer membrane calcium transporter VDAC2 is a new STING binding partner and the STING-VDAC2 interaction may regulate mitochondrial ROS/calcium levels.
justification: VDAC2, the mitochondrial outer-membrane calcium transporter, is a direct STING partner: STING reaches the mitochondrial calcium machinery, not only the ER's.

mechanism: STING depletion increases VDAC2/GRP75-mediated MERC formation
sentence: STING depletion potentiates VDAC2/GRP75-mediated MERC (mitochondria-ER contact) formation to increase mitochondrial ROS/calcium levels, impairs mitochondria function, and suppresses mTORC1/S6K signaling leading to RCC growth retardation.
justification: STING restrains VDAC2, so losing STING builds ER-mitochondria contacts and raises mitochondrial calcium; an innate-immunity-independent growth arm in renal cancer.

mechanism: co-immunoprecipitation in A498 and RCC10 cells
sentence: Binding of STING with VDAC2, ATP2A2, and ATP1A1 was confirmed in both A498 (Figure  3B; Figure S4B) and RCC10 (Figure 3C; Figure S4C, Supporting Information) tumor cells.
justification: Independent confirmation, in two renal carcinoma lines, that STING binds the ER calcium pump ATP2A2/SERCA2 — a second source for that edge.

mechanism: STING depletion raises mitochondrial calcium via VDAC2/GRP75 MERCs (opposite sign to PMID 40186485)
sentence: STING depletion potentiates VDAC2/GRP75-mediated MERC (mitochondria-ER contact) formation to increase mitochondrial ROS/calcium levels, impairs mitochondria function, and suppresses mTORC1/S6K signaling leading to RCC growth retardation.
justification: Here STING *limits* mitochondrial calcium, the opposite sign to the obese-atria study where STING knockdown relieved mitochondrial calcium overload: the direction of STING's effect on mitochondrial calcium is contested.

mechanism: ER stress relieves STIM1 retention; 11.5-fold increase in STING phosphorylation in mouse tumour models
sentence: Here, we developed an on-demand nanoparticle system that harnesses mitochondrial-ER functional interplay by concurrently inducing mtDNA release and ER stress, thereby relieving the STIM1-mediated brake on STING and enabling robust STING-TBK1 assembly and downstream signaling.
justification: Second therapeutic exploitation of the STIM1 brake: releasing it with ER stress, alongside mtDNA release, outperforms a clinical STING agonist, so the brake is a druggable amplifier.

mechanism: cardiomyocyte-specific STING knockout; gut microbial DNA no longer lowers Serca2 or contractility
sentence: In young lean StingDeltaCM mice, concomitant with their blunted inflammatory responses to microbial DNA accumulation, gut mEV treatment had minimal effects on Serca2 abundance and contractility in the heart ( Figures S4F ,  5E-G ).
justification: STING is required to downregulate SERCA2 in ageing cardiomyocytes, so STING controls the ER calcium pump at the expression level as well as by binding it: a route from DNA sensing to impaired calcium handling and contractility.

mechanism: IP3R1-GRP75-VDAC1 axis at MAMs; blocked by TGR5 agonism in Muller glia and DR rats
sentence: Mechanically, TGR5 blocked the IP3R1-GRP75-VDAC1 axis mediated Ca2+ efflux from the endoplasmic reticulum into mitochondria under diabetic condition.
justification: ITPR1 drives ER-to-mitochondria Ca2+ transfer through the IP3R1-GRP75-VDAC1 axis, the step that leads to mtDNA release and cGAS-STING activation in diabetic retinopathy.

mechanism: confocal colocalization of STIM1 puncta with ORAI1 in INS-1 cells under mitochondrial stress
sentence: Furthermore, STIM1 puncta colocalized with Orai1, suggesting Ca2+ influx through SOCE during mitophagy (Supplementary Fig.
justification: STIM1-ORAI1 assembly is triggered by mitophagy in beta-cells: ER-to-lysosome Ca2+ flux empties ER stores and recruits SOCE, a new upstream trigger for the STIM1 switch.

mechanism: DMXAA-induced Sjogren model; intravital GCaMP6f imaging of submandibular gland
sentence: Paradoxically, the Ca2+ levels achieved following neural stimulation in mice treated with DMXAA were enhanced despite significantly reduced fluid secretion.
justification: Pharmacological STING activation in vivo raises and spatially scrambles acinar Ca2+ signals, turning an apically confined rise into a global one: STING reshapes calcium signalling, not just its amplitude.
